chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Three (actions) with which Allah does not increase the Muslim except in honour: pardoning the one who oppressed him, giving to the one who deprived him, and maintaining kinship with the one who cut him off.
ai.seo_question: What three actions increase a Muslim's honor according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) identifies these three reciprocal virtues—pardoning the wrongdoer, giving to the withholding, and reconnecting with the severed—as means to elevate a Muslim's spiritual and social status. In Shia tradition, this is viewed not merely as passive tolerance but as active moral superiority that transforms weakness into divine honor (izz). This hadith is frequently cited in discussions on *adab* (etiquette) and the purification of the self from petty grudges.
